title: Existence of the normalized supported source for a diagonal projection
statement: theorem diagonalTrace_supportedSource_exists (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian (ProjectiveLine Y)] [IsNoetherian (diagonalSurface Y)] (hY : IsUnit (l : Γ(Y, ⊤))) [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l Y] [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l (ProjectiveLine Y)] [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l (diagonalSurface Y)] (D : DiagonalDerivedReduction l (diagonalScalarExtension l (diagonalSurface Y))) (δ : diagonalCompletedDomain l Y ⟶ diagonalCompletedCodomain l Y) (hδ : IsDiagonalLimit l Y hY D δ) (f : diagonalSurface Y ⟶ ProjectiveLine Y) (hf : f = pullback.fst (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) ∨ f = pullback.snd (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)) (t : Result l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) f) : Nonempty (SupportedSource l Y f t.Rc)

proof.text: Identify inverse image of the completed coefficient ring with the actual completed coefficient map through finite residue-ring projections; those projections also prove composition and identity coherence.

Compare diagonalTracePush with the identified-coefficient module direct image by identities on sections. Apply the tensor-normalized module composition theorem and the generic identity comparison, then the section equation. After forgetting modules this is exactly lowerStarComp followed by lowerStarCongr and lowerStarId. Apply it to the unit and transport along the named equality identifying the published completed source with the diagonal image. Component-wise forgetful comparisons and equality-transport lemmas establish the prescribed normalization.

The projective diagonal is closed; its open complement is quasi-compact since the ambient surface is Noetherian. Ringed open-closed exactness makes its ringed direct image exact. Scalar restriction retains the underlying abelian sheaf and is exact by exactness and reflection of the module-forgetful functors. Their composite diagonalTracePush is therefore exact.

The completed pushforward is right adjoint to the exact identified-coefficient inverse image, so it preserves K-injective complexes. Resolve a complex on the projective line by a K-injective complex and apply diagonal pushforward. Exactness gives a quasi-isomorphism, as does the composite with the projection since it is naturally the identity. Naturality of the derived unit, its K-injective computation clause and cancellation of invertible maps show that the derived unit is invertible on the diagonal image. Transfer along the single-complex comparison to obtain acyclicity of the actual supported source. Apply the normalized section isomorphism to the unit module and assemble SupportedSource.
